answer.why_different: The generated document appears to confuse the 3GPP notification-target URI placeholder with an OpenAPI callback runtime-expression key, and it emits both forms, producing duplicate callback entries. It also expands the notification schema inline and splits the error response into 4XX and 5XX responses instead of using the official reusable schema and default response.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP mapping defines notifyMOIDeletion as a POST to {notificationTarget}, and its request body contains the NotifyMoiDeletion fields, including href, notificationId, notificationType, eventTime, systemDN, and optional notification fields. Successful processing returns 204, while failure returns 4xx/5xx ErrorResponse.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI callback keys must be runtime expressions enclosed in braces, such as '{$request.body#/url}'. The runtime expression itself uses '$request.body#/...' and may reference a request-body property. Neither '{notificationTarget}' nor '$request.body#/notificationTarget' is a correctly formed callback-expression key.
answer.clearer_why: The official version defines one callback entry and uses a reusable NotifyMoiDeletion schema, making the callback structure less ambiguous. The generated version is more explicit about payload fields and separates 4XX/5XX responses, but its duplicate callback entries and malformed keys make the API harder to understand.

##### Runtime Expressions  
Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.
This mechanism is used by [Link Objects](#link-object) and [Callback Objects](#callback-object).  
The runtime expression is defined by the following [ABNF](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5234) syntax  
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
